clue.text: Military officer guarding extra-large stray

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, so the officer's letters go round the size

blocks.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A soldier's commanding officer keeps watch over a huge wandering animal.
explanation.walkthrough: L(OS)T: the size abbreviation sits inside the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray dog is one that has wandered from home, i.e. a lost animal, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: One's favourite island has vitality that's contagious

definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun: the answer is a contagious skin infection

blocks.note: one is = I am, contracted to I'M
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
I is the abbreviation for island
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: Someone's beloved island has a lively spirit that rubs off on visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' must be read as 'one is', the setter speaking as I. The definition is loose: 'that's contagious' points at a thing that is contagious.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a highly infectious bacterial skin disease, common among children.

clue.text: Old-style, you extracted teeth (not top)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is to be dropped
teeth that are extracted are pulled out and thrown about, so the remaining letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned dentist addresses a patient whose teeth have been pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the archaic object form of the second-person pronoun, used in old texts and the Bible.

clue.text: Continent holding back world money – delightful stuff!

indicators.note: back means read in the opposite direction, so the world and money run right to left
holding means the continent wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: the largest continent
an orb is a globe or sphere
M is a common abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A traveller enthuses about Asia storing up the world's wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delightful stuff' is loose but fair: the food of the gods stands for anything delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, and by extension anything delicious or delightful.

clue.text: A pull-out includes recipe, more than one in fact

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so the letters of the phrase before it are mixed
includes means the jumbled letters wrap round another letter

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A magazine's pull-out section contains a recipe, or in fact several.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull-out' reads as a supplement, but the hyphen hides the split: 'pull' is fodder and 'out' says to mix it.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a plural form denotes more than one of something.

clue.text: Meetings to resist cutting measures

indicators.note: something cutting into another thing ends up inside it

blocks.note: to counter is to oppose or resist
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A committee gathers to oppose proposed cuts in policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ens are printing measures, a crossword favourite alongside ems.
explanation.definitionFit: Encounters are meetings, often unexpected ones, so the plural nouns correspond.

clue.text: Foreign spy ring confiscates church film

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange, so the following word is rearranged
confiscating means taking something and holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church
a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An overseas espionage network seizes a reel of footage from a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy ring' reads as a single phrase but splits: 'spy' is mixed, 'ring' is O, and that whole takes in CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller, famous for its shower scene.

clue.text: 'Aspects of vice' lectures

blocks.note: first meaning: the gripping parts of a vice, the bench tool
second meaning: talks at length or scolds, informally

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Aspects of vice' look like a lecture title about wickedness; vice is the workshop clamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice has two jaws that grip the work, and to jaw is slang for lecturing someone at tedious length.

clue.text: It loves most precipitous hill starts

indicators.note: starts means only the opening letter of each of the words is used

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O; two of them
the initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Something adores the opening slopes of the steepest hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the definition: 'it' in the sense of sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'it' and the answer are informal words for sex appeal or attractive vitality.

clue.text: Pacific islands object about having to accept English ways

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the object is read backwards
accepting something means taking it in, so the turned word wraps the rest

blocks.note: an aim is an object or goal
E is the abbreviation for English
lanes are ways or roads

explanation.surface: Someone objects to adopting English customs in a group of Pacific islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' and 'ways' look like verb and customs, but they are a goal and roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanesia is the island region of the south-west Pacific including Fiji, Vanuatu and the Solomons.

clue.text: Revolutionary phase – article gets time wrong

blocks.note: the definite article
T is the abbreviation for time
an error is a wrong or mistake

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece gets the date of a stage in a revolution wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' looks like an anagram signal but is simply a noun meaning a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Terror (1793-94) was the period of mass executions during the French Revolution.

clue.text: Unlikely Oscar for 'Killers Working Together'

indicators.note: an unlikely version is an improbable rearrangement of the original

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film called Killers Working Together is an improbable Academy Award winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcas, or killer whales, hunt cooperatively in family pods.

clue.text: Attackers of Republican supporters

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
aiders are helpers or supporters

explanation.surface: Assailants come from among a party's own backers.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiders are those who make sudden attacks, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Toulouse-Lautrec took content that's oddly-numbered

definitions.note: adjective describing the right-hand page, which the answer names

indicators.note: content means what the phrase contains, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: spans the end of the painter's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: The painter Toulouse-Lautrec took something odd-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as happy, but it is the noun: what the phrase contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Recto is the right-hand page of a book, which always carries an odd page number.

clue.text: Airline holds suitable IC cert. for a type of energy

definitions.note: noun phrase for an adjective: the answer describes a type of energy

indicators.note: read as suit-able, able to be arranged to fit, so the letters are reordered
holds means the airline wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: El Al is Israel's national airline
taken as written

explanation.surface: An airline keeps an appropriate integrated-circuit certificate for some kind of power.
explanation.walkthrough: El Al, the Israeli carrier, splits in two around the mixed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical energy is one recognised form of energy, alongside kinetic, thermal and chemical.

clue.text: Nothing gets over pass ahead of northern city

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word for nothing is read backwards

blocks.note: nil means nothing
a col is a mountain pass
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Getting over a mountain pass leaves nothing before reaching a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of' joins the pass to N; the definition 'city' sits at the end with 'northern'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is a cathedral city in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Informal footwear on one backward holiday island

indicators.note: backward means the combined letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: sox is a casual spelling of socks
an means one

explanation.surface: Casual shoes worn by someone on a retrograde holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Naxos is the largest of the Cyclades, a Greek island popular with tourists.

clue.text: Secret clubs don't prevail

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to lose is to fail to prevail

explanation.surface: Secret societies fail to win the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as an adjective can mean secretive or reticent, as in keeping something close.

clue.text: Statecraft

blocks.note: the single printed word is read as two: state, then craft
first meaning: ...., the abbreviation for Arkansas
second meaning: a vessel, like Noah's

explanation.walkthrough: The single word statecraft splits into two halves, each a definition: a US state abbreviation and a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ark. is the standard abbreviation of Arkansas, and an ark is a ship or boat, most famously Noah's.

clue.text: Give up rugby player as a sweetener

blocks.note: to kick a habit is to give it up
backs are rugby players behind the forwards

explanation.surface: A rugby player is surrendered as an inducement to a rival club.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickback is an illicit payment, a bribe; a sweetener is likewise an inducement payment.

clue.text: Queen's favourite element: congress

blocks.note: Es is the chemical symbol for einsteinium
congress can mean sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: A queen's preferred component of political meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was the favourite of Elizabeth I; 'congress' means intercourse, not a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Essex was Queen Elizabeth I's famous favourite, often called simply Essex.

clue.text: Irregular Roman senate and people with nothing for queen on acid – deplorable

indicators.note: with one thing for another means swapping a letter out and putting a new one in its place
something deplorable is in a bad state, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: Senatus Populusque Romanus, the Roman motto
zero, shaped like O
Q is the abbreviation for queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone deplores irregular appearances of a queen on drugs in the Roman senate.
explanation.walkthrough: SPQR has its Q replaced by O, then the jumbled acid follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals, now and then.

clue.text: Moon-like ring associated with tribal revelry

indicators.note: revelry is wild partying, which throws the letters into disorder

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribe's ritual dancing in a moonlit ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon follows an orbit, so moon-like movement is orbital in nature.

clue.text: Watershed follows start of broadcast link

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: the initial letter
a watershed is a ridge dividing two river basins

explanation.surface: The TV watershed comes after the beginning of a broadcast connection.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the watershed is 9pm, after which adult TV may air; here it is the geographical ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge is a link or connection, literal or figurative, between two things.

clue.text: Live broadcast attempt is heartless frivolity

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
without its heart means the middle letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A live TV attempt lacks soul and is mere silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live broadcast' is a stock phrase, but 'broadcast' scatters the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity means lightness of manner or a lack of seriousness, as does frivolity.

clue.text: Thumb prodded into awkward person in government department

indicators.note: prodded into means pushed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a cuss is an awkward or cantankerous fellow
Tom Thumb, the tiny folk-tale hero

explanation.surface: A difficult civil servant gets a thumb poked into them.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs is the government body that collects import duties and controls goods at borders.

clue.text: Republic locks king out – 'It's over!'

indicators.note: the king is shut out, so his letter is dropped from the hair
over means turned over, so the little word is read backwards

blocks.note: locks of hair
R is for rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A republic bars its monarch and declares the reign finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks king out' reads as a coup, but 'locks' is hair; the 's is read as 'is', joining the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean republic, the first independent black republic, founded in 1804.

clue.text: Peg trembled without a top

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is removed

blocks.note: shook means trembled

explanation.surface: A hanging peg wobbled with no cap on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg and a hook are both fixtures for hanging things like coats.

clue.text: Bigwig hides underwear (surprise!) right in instrument

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked inside, so the bigwig wraps round the rest

blocks.note: a very important person
a bra is an undergarment
an exclamation of surprise
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A celebrity's concealed lingerie turns up inside a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Everything from the underwear to right sits between VI and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibraharp is another name for the vibraphone, a percussion instrument with metal bars.

clue.text: Special lifts to be installed in hospital recess

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the letters read upwards, in reverse
installed in means placed inside another piece

blocks.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
A&E is a hospital's accident and emergency department, the British emergency room

explanation.surface: Custom lifts are to be fitted in a hospital alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E, Britain's casualty department, stands for hospital with the ampersand dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess, usually vaulted, at the end of a church.

clue.text: Society cuts bank job

indicators.note: something that cuts into another goes inside it

blocks.note: the pot is the bank or pool of money in a game
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A society's cuts are hitting jobs at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a position of employment, a job.

clue.text: Debauched feature of corgi a sticking-point

indicators.note: a feature of something is part of it, so the letters are within the words

blocks.note: runs across three words of the phrase

explanation.surface: A dissolute aspect of a corgi turns out to be a sticking-point.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic describes wild, unrestrained revelry, i.e. debauchery.

clue.text: Southern food plants

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
pies are food

explanation.surface: Plants in a southern garden yield food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' looks botanical but means agents placed to gather secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is a person placed undercover in an organisation, i.e. a spy.
